subject: group analysis error for missing category

messages.author: efabcb964855e79a
messages.subject: group analysis error for missing category
parts:
Hi,

I am conducting a multiple group analysis among survey respondents and receive the following error:

"lavaan ERROR: some categories of variable `C1d' are empty in group 2; frequencies"

When I checked responses to question 'C1d' I found that none of the survey respondents in group 2 chose category 4 - "Strongly disagree", whereas
other groups chose answers across all categories.

Is this question unusable or is there a way to get lavaan to work through this?

Thanks for any assistance

Matt

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: group analysis error for missing category
parts:
When I checked responses to question 'C1d' I found that none of the survey respondents in group 2 chose category 4 - "Strongly disagree", whereas
other groups chose answers across all categories.

Is this question unusable or is there a way to get lavaan to work through this?

I've run into the same problem using other software as well (Mplus, LISREL).  As far as I know, you will need to collapse the categories in the other groups so they have the same number of categories as in group 2.  Something I haven't tried, though, is adding a single observation to group 2, which would have C1d == 4 and missing values for all other variables.  That might trick the program into recognizing 4 categories when it estimates thresholds and subsequently the polychoric correlation matrix, but I'm not sure it will work.

Terry

messages.author: 6a75f6f91a59c568
messages.subject: Re: group analysis error for missing category
parts:
Matt,

If particular responses were 'Strongly agree' to 'Strongly disagree', You may can convert numerical (integer) vector; Like Likert Scale, 1 to 5 or 1 to 7.

If NA value appeared within converted vectors, You may fill NA values.

But, Without NA values, You may try to collapse Agree or Disagree.

Question: Your main advices were collapsing the first category into the second, and the last category into second last. So, I have a one more question. Can I convert this item responses to dichotomous type to save degree of freedom?
 
Answer: You can do this of course, but you'll lose the property of you test being polytomous and ordered (and as a consequence lose precision when trying to estimate θ, if that's your end goal). How you try and dichotomize the data will also affect the fit statistics as well as the estimated parameters, so it's not entirely clear what the best way to dichotomize is. I would recommend trying to preserve the nature of your test to the best of your ability, since in the end that's likely what you are trying to understand. Collapsing from 7 to 5 categories isn't unheard of in the literature, but reviewers may have a bigger issue when going from 7 to only 2. Cheers. 
https://groups.google.com/d/msg/mirt-package/0fG60G8chzY/4jWwdOlUimoJ

Seongho Bae

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: group analysis error for missing category
parts:
This seems like an interesting phenomenon, and is something I thought about a while back as well (I'm somewhat surprised to hear it exists in Mplus and LISREAL though). What happens when estimating intercept parameters in multiple group settings where one group has no instantiations of a relevant category is that no information about the parameter estimate can come from that respective group (e.g., when maximizing the likelihood, all the likelihood information comes from only one group instead of two). This isn't to say that it doesn't exist, it's just that it doesn't exist in isolation when considering one group at a time, and this can cause issues for estimators which need intercept and covariance parameters to be identified for each group. Basically, the idea is to set the parameter estimates equal across group so that they can be uniquely identified, but for the group without the category of interest the parameter is really just a placeholder since all the information comes from other sources. I've attached an example which doesn't require collapsing the data arbitrarily to get around this, and I imagine lavaan could do something like this as well (at least with the MML estimator, not sure about the others). Cheers.

Phil
